title: Rigidity and Stiffness in Parkinson's
content: Rigidity refers to muscle stiffness and is a common movement feature of Parkinson's disease. It can occur in the arms, legs, neck or trunk and may contribute to reduced range of motion, discomfort and difficulty with everyday movement. Rigidity can sometimes contribute to changes in posture, walking and arm swing. Muscle stiffness alone does not establish Parkinson's disease because stiffness can occur for many other reasons. Persistent or unexplained stiffness, particularly when accompanied by other movement changes, should be discussed with an appropriate healthcare professional.
